comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
You gotta work on your optimization, and not hide behind "well I have more players than others".

The main trick is to not show things you don't need to show. Lower quality models, update the logic less often and not in the visual update loop, don't render things that aren't even on screen and so on.

I think what I'm seeing is impressive except for the frame rate.

replies.author: codeninja
replies.body:
Im tuning LOD and stepping between positioning when the models are too far to decent details. Its a process of tradeoffs. Here though everything is forced rendered due to my density and proximity. 

The same scene ran at like three frames per second before optimizations.

comments.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
comments.body:
this is not "a little laggy" if I were running a game this poorly with mods my thoughts would be "Oh I definitely have too many mods running, I need to optimise this by removing some of the heavier ones or a LOT of the smaller ones." If this were a game with no mods I would be be trying to optimise my settings to the bare minimum.

Now bear in mind that I know absolutely nothing about game dev, and I do understand that anything with this many players is going to be insanely hard to optimise.

Here's some questions that I think you need to think about: How likely do you think it is that tens of thousands of people are going to be playing your game for years to come? Do you really need to be aiming for 1K players?

How many "players" are in this screenshot:

https://preview.redd.it/xvr21po83zth1.png?width=1913&format=png&auto=webp&s=8ffc440d135a337b6151b534fd25154f1470892a

Follow up to that; Is this readable at all, or is it just a hugely convoluted mess for the sake of being a convoluted mess? What would this look like if it was scaled down to 500 player lobbies and how much easier is it to optimise for that amount?

  
Not saying this to be snarky or mean at all, even if it's optimised this doesn't seem like it would be sustainably fun for the majority of players especially if it's anything like an [agar.io](http://agar.io) or [snake.io](http://snake.io) type game where you start small and kill other players to get bigger. That will just push a ton of people out, and you'll be ending up with smaller lobbies anyway. Could it be more feasible to go for 500, and then have some type of passive "food" that doesn't take up as much resources?

I hope you take these comments as feedback and constructive criticism rather than just shitting on you lol. It's just kind of hard to image what the gameplay is like, if the footage is this janky and chaotic to begin with you know? Hard to tell what the potential is here, and the average player is probably going to feel that too

replies.author: codeninja
replies.body:
This is my demo arena where I can throw up a bunch of characters and have them automatically walk around and test for camera and terrain glitches.

So from that perspective, no, this is not supposed to be fun. Nor entertaining. It's a demo stage test bed playground...

I think you're absolutely correct. I don't think a thousand people are going to be joining a match. I will be surprised if a thousand people total play this game... somewhere on a hundred players per side is probably where i'm going to end up landing.

Team based point capture shooter is the direction i'm taking it.

I do appreciate your feedback thank you.
